messages.subject: Access to files with Rapache
messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues!
I try to run a R script from Rapache and I have this error

###############################################################
RApache Warning/Error!!!
In file(file, "r") : cannot open file '/home/luis/world.asc':
Permission denied
###############################################################

where world.asc is a raster map imported to R with the function
import.asc (package adehabitat)

world <- import.asc("/home/luis/world.asc")

 Does anybody knows what is going wront? I feel that I have to give
permissions to Rapache to read and write files in my hard disk,
but...where and how?

Thanks in advance...

Luis R.

messages.subject: Re: Access to files with Rapache
messages.body_plain:
This is almost certainly a simple Unix user permissions issue. The
rapache process - i.e., the httpd process -- is being run as some user,
probably httpd or apache. That user has to be able to read the file.

A simple way to deal with that is

$ chmod g+r /home/luis/world.asc

See man chmod for what that means.

messages.subject: Problem Configuring RApache on OS X 10.5.8
messages.subject_clean: Problem Configuring RApache on OS X 10.5.8
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

I've been trying to get RApache set up properly on my Macbook Pro
running OS X 10.5.8.  After installing RApache successfully (I think),
I added the following to the httpd.conf file as suggested.

# All Apache modules are loaded this way. The most important thing to
# remember is that the string "R_module" is case sensitive, so get it
# right in the config file.

LoadModule R_module           /apache/module/path/mod_R.so

# Place this in the config file to turn error messages into HTML which
# are printed in the browser. Without this, all warning and error
messages
# are printed to the Apache error log file.

ROutputErrors

# Prints out a nice report about R running within Apache
<Location /RApacheInfo>
	SetHandler r-info
</Location>

With these additions, I was then able to successfully go to
http://localhost/RApacheInfo and see the status information.
If I add the following additional line,

REvalOnStartup "library(brew)"

I can no longer successfully load the RApacheInfo page successfully.
I don't know what the issue is here.

Any thoughts as to what I might be doing wrong?

Chris
